The *Dvinnaṁbuddhānaṁanuppajjamānapañha* ("Why Must There Be Only One Buddha At A Time?") is a discourse within the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.1.1) [SuttaCentral]. The text addresses the classical doctrinal problem of why two fully enlightened Buddhas do not arise in the world at the same time [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes thematic and doctrinal connections to several earlier canonical and paracanonical treatments of this topic, including the *Sampasādanīya Sutta* (DN 28), the *Bahudhātuka Sutta* (MN 115), the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttaranikāya* (AN 1.277), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 16), and the *Vicayahārasampāta* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 21) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes three translations of the text in three languages [SuttaCentral].
